# ScrollProgress
Atlas Scroll Progress v1 — a thin bar that shows how far the reader has scrolled through a page or a scrollable container. 2 orientations × 2 scopes × 3 drawn levels (0, 50, 100), 12 in total; the level is drawn as a variant only because Figma cannot show a live scroll value — in code it follows scroll position continuously.

When to use: long articles, docs and reading views where "how far through am I" helps. When not to use: for task, upload or step progress (use Progress), for content that is still loading (use Skeleton or Spinner), or as the only sign of position on a short page.

Scope=page is a flat, full-width strip pinned to the top edge of the viewport; Scope=container is a rounded bar or rail placed by the caller along the scrollable element it tracks. Orientation=vertical is a rail whose fill grows downward. The fill eases with duration/fast and easing/standard; under prefers-reduced-motion it follows scroll with no ease. Decorative by default (hidden from assistive tech); give it an aria-label to expose it as a progressbar.

## API

```tsx
import { ScrollProgress } from "@atlas/ui-web/primitives/ScrollProgress/ScrollProgress"
```

**ScrollProgress** — also accepts native `<div>` attributes (except children, role)
- ref: not forwarded — `ref` does not type-check; reach the element by `id`
- `orientation?: ScrollProgressOrientation`
- `scope?: ScrollProgressScope`
- `target?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null>`
- `axis?: ScrollProgressAxis`
